LESSON: ZACCHAEUS THE TAX COLLECTOR

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible Bible Stories:
Topic 2.2: Zacchaeus the Tax Collector

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Zacchaeus the Tax Collector. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the story of Zacchaeus,
2. recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour positively,
3. demonstrate integrity when using money,
4. discuss why it is important to repent sins in order to be like Christ. The learner is guided to: tree and share the drawings with peers, from bad behaviour//sin, the story of Zacchaeus, Christ as the saviour. How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. retell the story of Zacchaeus,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to retell the story of Zacchaeus,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour positively,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour positively,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. demonstrate integrity when using money,

4. discuss why it is important to repent sins in order to be like Christ. The learner is guided to: tree and share the drawings with peers, from bad behaviour//sin, the story of Zacchaeus, Christ as the saviour. How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?

The learner is guided to: tree and share the drawings with peers, from bad behaviour//sin, the story of Zacchaeus, Christ as the saviour. How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Zacchaeus the Tax Collector.
2. Explain Zacchaeus the Tax Collector to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: read Luke19:2-10 in turns,
4. Show that you can: retell the story of Zacchaeus,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Zacchaeus the Tax Collector. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read Luke19:2-10 in turns,
2. Draw and colour Zacchaeus on a tree and share the drawings with peers,

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. retell the story of Zacchaeus,
2. recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour positively,
3. demonstrate integrity when using money,
4. discuss why it is important to repent sins in order to be like Christ. The learner is guided to: tree and share the drawings with peers, from bad behaviour//sin, the story of Zacchaeus, Christ as the saviour. How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
